root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `Cleanup()` may probe the tracked single-colon auxiliary-path suffix with `strncmp(&*it, "://", 3)`, the suffix starting at `it` must contain at least the three bytes the source-level compare requests.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the tracked single-colon candidate with `remaining_bytes=1` and still executes the `://` probe, matching the saved AddressSanitizer crash. The authoritative `-fix` image suppresses that probe entirely by computing `remaining = std::distance(in.end(), it)`, so the original and closest `:aa` perturbation remain guarded and never yield a genuine fixed-side probe witness for the intended length obligation.
root_cause_criterion.evidence_limitation: The authoritative fixed image at commit `3664fe20c07fdbd4d72c5caf68375b056806ab08` still reaches the same single-colon candidate class but records `remaining_bytes=-1` on the original input and `remaining_bytes=-3` on the closest `:aa` perturbation, with no `cleanup_colon_probe` events in either case. That makes the source-level length obligation selected and frozen here, but not differentially repair-verified by the provided fixed assets.

nodes.state: On the original witness, the tracked single-colon suffix reaches `strncmp(&*it, "://", 3)` with `probe_width=3` and only `remaining_bytes=1`, so the source-level compare attempts to read past the available suffix.

edges.relation: The same tracked suffix pointer selected at the vulnerable loop iteration is the pointer passed unchanged into the crashing `strncmp` probe.
